thread:
Acme Support: Hey team, our integration started failing this morning when calling the embeddings endpoint. We get a 400 with: "Invalid embedding dimension: expected 1536 got 768". We're calling model=redwood-emb-1536 via the hosted API. Payload is a JSON array of strings. Example curl we used:

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-emb-1536","input":["hello world"]}'

Acme Support: This worked yesterday, no code changes on our side. Traffic is a mix of single items and small batches. Any quick suggestions? Our release is blocked.

Priya R: thanks for flagging — can you paste the full error response (including request_id) and the exact model string from the request? also which client library/version are you using?

Acme Support: request_id: req_0a7f3b2c, model in logs is exactly "redwood-emb-1536". We're using a thin wrapper around curl (no SDK). Full server response:

{
  "error": "Invalid embedding dimension: expected 1536 got 768",
  "request_id": "req_0a7f3b2c"
}

Jared L: hunch — this looks like a dimension mismatch between model choice and the vector produced by upstream transformation or a routing to a different model variant. Can you confirm the response payload shape? sometimes clients accidentally send pre-computed vectors to the embeddings endpoint instead of raw text (hence smaller dim). Also, do you see batching of multiple input arrays in one request?

Acme Support: we definitely send text only. Here's the exact request body logged at our edge: 

{"model":"redwood-emb-1536","input":["order #123 status update","refund policy"]}

Logs show the same. No precomputed vectors on our side.

Marta (docs): quick doc note — we should add a clear FAQ entry: "Why am I seeing dimension errors?" with mapping table (model -> expected dim) and a recommendation to check you aren't double-encoding. I can draft if you confirm cause.

Kai: tagging @eng-runtime — we saw a subtle batching issue last week on Dedicated where single-item batches could be routed to a compact model variant (768) if kernel selection logic mis-identified sequence length. Investigating whether routing rules mistakenly matched redwood-emb-1536 to a 768-compatible backend under certain autoscale conditions.

Kai: repro steps I ran locally: send 1-item arrays at high QPS with intermittent 2-item batches; if batcher merges slightly different shapes we saw dimension coercion downstream. Quick check: can you try forcing a single input (no array) payload to see if behavior differs? e.g. {"model":"redwood-emb-1536","input":"hello world"} and paste result.

Acme Support: tried single-string (not array), same error and request_id req_0a7f3c1. We also toggled to a different region and got same.

Jared L: ok that's useful. Priya and I will collect server-side logs for req_0a7f3b2c and req_0a7f3c1. Kai, please confirm if a hotfix is needed to the batching router.

Priya R: Runbook checklist I'm following and asking you to confirm (customer-facing steps we can send now):
- gather request_id, full request body, response body (done).
- confirm model string and client version (done).
- try call with model redwood-emb-768 to see if that succeeds (quick workaround).
- provide throughput pattern (QPS, payload sizes) — Acme, can you paste a short sample of recent requests per second?
- attach any edge proxy logs that may modify payloads (e.g., form encoding).

Acme Support: QPS ~120 for embeddings, 70% single-item, 30% 2-4 item batches. No proxy modifying JSON.

Kai: thanks. Preliminary finding: router sometimes normalizes compatible models and will fallback to a lower-dim compute when autoscaling to fill capacity. That's a bug — should never change model numeric signature. I'm opening an eng ticket. For immediate mitigation, you can: 
- point customer to model redwood-emb-768 (if their app can accept 768 dims) OR
- pin routing to a higher-tier pool using the header X-Redwood-Pool: dedicated-high (for customers on Dedicated) OR
- set smaller batch_size so router doesn't coalesce across different shapes.

Jared L: adding concrete repro curl that we used to trigger locally (logs attached):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-emb-1536","input":["A","B","C"]}'

Then immediately follow with several single-item requests. After ~30s we saw returned dim 768 and a 400.

Marta (docs): I'll prepare two docs changes:
- FAQ entry with mapping table and quick fixes (pin model, batch_size changes, example error message).
- Support runbook checklist + template customer message. Drafting now, will link PR.

Priya R: customer-facing note (please review before we send):
"Hi — thanks for the report. We identified a router bug that can, in high-throughput mixed-batch patterns, return embeddings from a lower-dimension compute path. Short-term workarounds: 1) call redwood-emb-768 if your app accepts 768-dim vectors, 2) reduce batch_size or avoid mixing single-item and multi-item requests, or 3) set routing header to pin to high-capacity pool (if on Dedicated). Our eng team is deploying a fix; ETA ~2 hours. We'll follow up when it's live and update a runbook / FAQ. — Priya, Redwood Support"

Kai: I'll own the fix and rollout, thanks. Creating eng issue ENG-4532 and a hotfix branch now. Will post once deployed.

docs-bot: Created PR 432 for FAQ + runbook draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/432

Jared L: once Kai confirms deployment, we'll validate with customer by sending a controlled test and closing the ticket. Also adding a short note for billing: no extra charges expected from retries here, but advise customer on best-effort retries/backoff.

Acme Support: thanks — we'll try the 768 fallback to unblock our release and stand by for the fix. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Priya R: summary/action items:
- Kai / eng-runtime: deploy hotfix (owner: Kai).
- Marta/docs: land PR with FAQ and runbook (owner: Marta).
- Support: communicate workaround to customer (owner: Priya).
- Postmortem & monitoring rule: trigger alert if dimension-mismatch errors > 0.1% of embeddings requests (owner: Jared).

Jared L: I'll add the alert to the console and attach a dashboard with example traces. Closing thread for now; will update when eng confirms deploy.

Acme Support: confirmed fallback to redwood-emb-768 worked for now. Leaving ticket open until fix is live. Thank you.

(End of thread)
